events.title: A second mobile operator
events.description: Wataniya Mobile (today Ooredoo Palestine) launches in the West Bank, adding competition to a market that Jawwal had led on its own.

events.title: Agreement on frequencies
events.description: An agreement over the 2100 MHz frequency band is reached, which later makes it possible to switch on 3G.

events.title: Ooredoo reaches Gaza
events.description: The second operator begins offering services in the Gaza Strip, giving people there another mobile option.

events.title: 3G reaches the West Bank
events.description: On 23 January 2018, 3G launched in the West Bank following the agreement over radio frequencies. It was not available in Gaza at that time.

events.title: Mostly mobile access
events.description: Around 71% of people had internet access, but only about 7% had a fixed-broadband subscription, so most people relied on mobile networks to get online.

events.title: COVID-19 moves life online
events.description: After schools and universities closed in March 2020, the Ministry of Education launched distance learning, and the internet became essential for study and work.

events.title: The Digital West Bank and Gaza project
events.description: The World Bank approved a $20 million grant to expand fibre-optic networks and build e-government services, aiming to close infrastructure gaps.

events.title: A framework for 4G and 5G
events.description: Israel and the Palestinian Authority agree a framework intended to allow 4G and 5G mobile technology in the future.

events.title: Most people are online
events.description: About 88.6% of people in Palestine are internet users (around 4.82 million), with roughly 4.46 million mobile connections.

events.title: Approval for 4G
events.description: A 4G upgrade for the West Bank is approved as part of the 2022 framework, with rollout expected within months.
